theorem_statement: The primitive CLXV set {1,5,12,8} union {3,6,9} is the projective completion of AG(2,2). The J-cycle gives the four affine points, the q-axis gives the three points at infinity, and the seven affine/projective lines form the Fano plane PG(2,2).
interpretive_note: This explains the Fano bridge: the stabilizer quarter-turn dynamics and the q-axis are not merely two lists summing to seven. They are the affine square and its three directions at infinity. The line at infinity is exactly the missing decimal q-axis {3,6,9}.
